title: Sweden Says 'Hej då' to Phones in Class!
summary: Have you ever tried to do homework while your phone buzzes with notifications? It's super hard to focus! Sweden thinks so too. Starting this fall, the country will ban mobile phones in all schools. That means no phones during class—at all. Sweden used to be a champion of digital learning. It's home to Spotify and Ericsson, and its schools are packed with laptops and tablets. But now the government is hitting the rewind button. Why? Because reading levels are dropping. In a big international test, almost one in four Swedish 9th graders couldn't read well enough. The government believes books and pencils are better for learning. They even set aside $59 million to buy new textbooks. At Malmö Borgarskola high school, phones are already banned. Students drop them in a box called the 'Mobile Hotel' and pick them up after class. 'When you have a phone, there's always something to look at,' says Melina, 17. 'It's less of a distraction.' Her classmate Vasilije agrees: 'Games are more fun than learning, so taking away phones helps.' But not everyone is happy. Some experts worry that kids won't learn digital skills they'll need for future jobs. Still, Sweden is also telling parents to have screen-free zones at home. Even little kids under 2 should only use books and non-digital toys. It's a big experiment—will going old-school make kids smarter? We'll find out!
why_it_matters: This story may make you think about how you use your own phone or tablet during homework time, and why sometimes putting devices away can help your brain focus better.

background_read: Sweden (a country in Northern Europe) is famous for its tech companies like Spotify (a music app) and Ericsson (a maker of mobile technology). In the past, Sweden pushed for lots of computers in classrooms.
Now many countries are wondering if too much screen time harms learning. Studies show that reading books on paper helps kids remember better than reading on screens.
Article_Structure: WHO: Sweden's government, students like Melina and Vasilije, and school Malmö Borgarskola.
WHAT: A ban on mobile phones during all classes, plus money to buy new textbooks instead.
WHERE: Throughout Sweden, including high schools that already use 'Mobile Hotel' boxes.
WHY: Reading levels are dropping — nearly 1 in 4 ninth graders couldn't read well enough — and officials believe phones are a big distraction.

perspectives.description: Many students and teachers feel the ban will help everyone concentrate better and improve reading skills.
Some tech experts worry that kids won't be prepared for a digital future if they don't learn to use technology responsibly in school.
The experiment shows how societies are trying to balance the benefits of technology with the need for deep, focused learning.
